Analytic cross-check: target wz[0] = 0.430318/0.499050/0.323298 = w0*sqrt(1+(s/zR)^2) with zR = pi*w0^2/(lambda*Mp2) = 78.737 mm, exactly the encoded geometry's prediction; test-1 target focus z=249.85 = L1 + 49.85, the ABCD image of a waist 50 mm before an f=50 lens. verdicts.reproduction: Reproduced all three variants myself (shimmed joint runner). (a) Self-consistent fftfreq(N+1, d=L/N) + Fresnel TF: FAILS all 3 tests; measured P2 rel errors 3.10e-3/1.61e-3/1.91e-3 vs allclose allowance (atol-dominated) 1.43e-3/8.5e-4/7.8e-4. (b) fftfreq(N+1, d=L/(N+1)) (spacing 1/L) + Fresnel TF: PASSES, P2 rel err down to 2.4e-16. (c) Exact angular-spectrum kernel with the same 1/L spacing: PASSES. So the kernel is not the discriminator, only the unstated frequency spacing. The grids are genuinely mutually inconsistent: P1 target = pi*w0^2 to 2.8e-12 pins the SPATIAL grid to linspace(-L/2,L/2,N+1) (dx=L/N), while P2 pins the FREQUENCY grid to df=1/L; no single sampling convention yields both. Stronger than first pass: the exact analytic free-space solution |E|=(w0/w)exp(-r^2/w^2) fails ALL 3 tests (rel err -3.5e-3/-1.6e-3/-2.5e-2), so the targets encode the author's discrete FFT artifact (incl. window truncation/wrap-around), not the physics; nothing in prompt/background/docstring states the discretization.

fix.before: The calculation needs to be done in fourier domain and the final result should be in time domain.
fix.after: The calculation needs to be done in fourier domain and the final result should be in time domain. Sample the field on x = np.linspace(-L/2, L/2, N+1) (spacing L/N) and use spatial frequencies with spacing 1/L, i.e. fx = np.fft.fftfreq(N+1, d=L/(N+1)), with the Fresnel transfer function H = exp(-1j*np.pi*Ld*z*(fx**2+fy**2)).
fix.side_effects: No target change. Alternative (weaker): loosen the test comparison to ~5e-3 relative on (P1,P2) so both common spacings pass - but the analytic solution would still fail test 3 (2.5e-2 off), so the prompt_edit is the honest fix.

verdicts.reproduction: Verified the targets myself: test-1 target P1 = 3.141592653581e-06 = pi*w0^2 (rel diff 2.8e-12), test-2 rel diff 8.6e-14 -> unit PEAK amplitude E0=exp(-r^2/w0^2) is what the targets encode (test 3's 3.1e-4 offset is just window truncation of the same unit-peak field, matched to 1e-14 by the discrete sum). Unit-total-power normalization variant (sum|E|^2 dA = 1): FAILS all 3 tests (ran it). The background explicitly writes E = c/omega(z) * exp(...) with 'c is a constant' never given, and the docstring says only 'absolute value of the beam's amplitude distribution' - keeping the literal 1/omega(z) prefactor with c=1 gives peak 1/w0 and P1 = pi*w0, also wrong. Confidence medium (kept from first pass): unit-peak is the most common default in FFT beam-propagation code, so many solvers land on it naturally, but it is strictly an unstated choice.

summary: All 9 first-pass findings reproduce exactly and are confirmed at their original severities: the simps import (D12) zeroes all three steps under official scoring before any solver code runs, and behind a shim each step still hides an author-private convention (28.1: df=1/L frequency spacing inconsistent with the dx=L/N spatial grid, plus unit-peak normalization of an unspecified constant; 28.2: docstring geometry that scores 0/3 while targets encode absolute-z/waist-at-s/lens-at-L1, matched to 1.7e-16; 28.3: 'Intensity' target that is actually an amplitude map, grid-argmin focus, and a 16-um-window unit slip baked into the frozen arrays). One small strengthening: the exact analytic free-space solution fails ALL three 28.1 tests, not just test 3. The problem is fixable to fair with moderate effort and zero target regeneration: one dependency-string fix plus four doc/prompt edits (28.2 geometry, 28.1 discretization+normalization, 28.3 amplitude-vs-intensity and focus convention) make every confirmed target derivable; the two remaining minors (permutation-invariant 28.1 tests, 16-um window) only need fixing if false positives / unit honesty matter.
